subject: Cannot evaluate rstan::log_prob on stanfit object passed to parallel nodes

messages.author: 2ffa956ce2411d70
messages.subject: Cannot evaluate rstan::log_prob on stanfit object passed to parallel nodes
parts:
Dear all,

My goal is to evaluate rstan::log_prob() on a fitted Stan object (i.e., of class 'stanfit') in parallel using a cluster created with parallel::makeCluster().

The problem is that calling log_prob() on the model on the nodes (after exporting the stanfit object) produces the following error:
the model object is not created or not valid

I have tried a variety of things (trying to compile the object again on the nodes by calling rstan::sampling or rstan::stan_model), but nothing has worked so far. Any help would be very much appreciated. Below follows some example code exemplifying the problem.

Cheers,
Henrik


library(rstan)
# model
stancode <- 'data {
  int<lower=1> N; // number of observations
  vector[N] y; // observations
}
parameters {
  real<lower=0> sigma2;
}
model {
  target += cauchy_lpdf(sigma2 | 1, 1) - cauchy_lccdf(0 | 1, 1);
  target += normal_lpdf(y | 0, sqrt(sigma2));
}
'
stanmodel <- stan_model(model_code = stancode, model_name="stanmodel")


# generate data
set.seed(1)
N <- 5
sigma2_gen <- 1
y <- rnorm(N, sd = sqrt(sigma2_gen))


# fit model
stanobject <- sampling(stanmodel, data = list(y = y, N = N))
pars <- extract(object = stanobject, par = c("sigma2", "lp__"))
sigma2_t <- log(pars$sigma2)  # unconstrained pars


log_prob(stanobject, sigma2_t[1])
# [1] -7.545463


require(parallel)
cl <- makeCluster(2, useXDR = FALSE)


clusterEvalQ(cl, require(rstan))
clusterExport(cl = cl, varlist = c("stanobject", "sigma2_t"))
clusterEvalQ(cl, log_prob(stanobject, sigma2_t[1]))
# Error in checkForRemoteErrors(lapply(cl, recvResult)) :
#   2 nodes produced errors; first error: the model object is not created or not valid


stopCluster(cl)

messages.author: 2ffa956ce2411d70
messages.subject: Re: Cannot evaluate rstan::log_prob on stanfit object passed to parallel nodes
parts:
Is there no way to recompile the model from a stanfit object that contains samples? 

My reason for being a little bit persistent on this issue is that I encounter basically the same problem when trying to call rstan::log_prob() on a model estimated on a different computer (with different OS). Right now it appears that the only way to deal with this latter problem is to compile a new stanfit object (without samples). Importantly, it appears I am only able to recompile the new version of the model before loading the model with samples fitted on a different computer.

messages.subject: Re: Cannot evaluate rstan::log_prob on stanfit object passed to parallel nodes
parts:
On Saturday, March 25, 2017 at 3:55:16 PM UTC-4, Henrik Singmann wrote:
Is there no way to recompile the model from a stanfit object that contains samples? 

My reason for being a little bit persistent on this issue is that I encounter basically the same problem when trying to call rstan::log_prob() on a model estimated on a different computer (with different OS). Right now it appears that the only way to deal with this latter problem is to compile a new stanfit object (without samples). Importantly, it appears I am only able to recompile the new version of the model before loading the model with samples fitted on a different computer.

Yeah, none of that is supported by rstan currently. The design problem is that the log_prob() method is defined for a stanfit object, when it should be defined for an instantiated stanmodel object, but there is no concept of an instantiated stanmodel object currently.

Ben

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Cannot evaluate rstan::log_prob on stanfit object passed to parallel nodes
parts:
> On Mar 25, 2017, at 4:29 PM, Henrik Singmann <sing...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> That is sad.

I think this is slated to be generalized in Stan 3, but
we haven't really started working on that yet.

> Yeah, none of that is supported by rstan currently. The design problem is that the log_prob() method is defined for a stanfit object, when it should be defined for an instantiated stanmodel object, but there is no concept of an instantiated stanmodel object currently.

What gets created by stan_model()? Is that just a fit object
with no MCMC draws or data?

Would it be hard to have an object specifically for a model
instantiated with data? That's what we want to use for the log
density and gradient calcs. And maybe we'll eventually make the
data mutable to support more flexible algorithm development.

The pipeline that the C++ interface to Stan forces on interfaces is
basically:

1. stan program -> c++ class -> instantiated object code

2. data + c++ class -> c++ class instance

3. data + inits + seeds + other config -> MCMC draws object

Step (3) can be replaced with optimization, diagnostis, ADVI, etc.

- Bob

messages.author: 2ffa956ce2411d70
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Cannot evaluate rstan::log_prob on stanfit object passed to parallel nodes
parts:
Our current usecase is the following (an extension of what is available here https://cran.r-project.org/package=bridgesampling):

1. Users program their model and obtain samples from the posterior.
2. They pass the fitted model with the samples to our functions. We extract the posteriors samples on the unconstrained scale from the object.
3. We evaluate log_prob with old (i.e., posterior draws) and new samples on the unconstrained scale.

Right now one problem is that when the model is fitted (i.e., step 1) on a different PC, we cannot use the model object for evaluating log_prob. We can only use it to extract the samples on the constrained scale. For obtaining the unconstrained samples and running log_prob() we need a newly created stanfit object (without samples), However, we cannot recreate it from the model once it is loaded.

For an implementation of this see: https://github.com/quentingronau/bridgesampling/tree/stan_interface
Function: stan_bridge_sampler()

So we can get it to work with the current version, but it is not super convenient.

Cheers,
Henrik (and Quentin)

Thanks for the rundown of what you're trying to do. It's
helpful as we think about design for Stan 3.

You need a model class instantiated with data for log
density and constraining/unconstraining transforms. That
involves platform-specific object code, so no way to port
cross platform without recompiling. Right now, you have
to roll that into a dummy fit object, which isn't really doing
any extra work, but the code's opaque and clunky (I believe
"smells bad" is the technical term for code that needs to
be refactored).

One thing RStan could potentially do is reflect the Stan model structure
with transforms into an R object. It would need the compiled
model to do that initially. The C++ API would need to be generalized
to make that available more granularly---right now it's code
generated to do all the transforms at once. But we need to do that
anyway to make the C++ code for models more useful.

- Bob
